description: Multi-host pivot demonstration — the canonical S14 reference. Exercises real SSH lateral movement between three networked hosts (attacker → target1 → target2) on a private Docker bridge. Every technique runs on a declared host and produces per-host evidence. This closes the gap the predecessor artifact documented but never demonstrated in published evidence (single-host examples only).

context_contract.purpose: Preserve declared benign administrative traffic separately from attack transitions.

background_activities.purpose: Declared security-telemetry heartbeat; it must not be counted as command-and-control or exfiltration.
Declared maintenance traffic; it must remain distinguishable from the later lateral payload transfer.

techniques.name: Network Service Discovery
techniques.description: From the attacker host, probe target1 for an open SSH service.

techniques.name: Brute Force: Password Guessing
techniques.description: Lab pre-stages a weak password on target1; the attacker iterates a tiny wordlist until it succeeds.

techniques.name: Remote Services: SSH
techniques.description: Real SSH session from attacker to target1 with the guessed password. Captures the remote uname.

techniques.name: File and Directory Discovery
techniques.description: Once on target1, enumerate the filesystem to plan further movement.

techniques.name: Lateral Tool Transfer
techniques.description: Stage a tiny shell payload on the attacker, push it to target2 via SCP/SSH using the lab-pre-staged credentials.

techniques.name: Command and Scripting Interpreter: Unix Shell
techniques.description: Execute the dropped payload on target2 over SSH; capture stdout as evidence of cross-host code execution.
